Alright, let me think this through. I've been farming this land for fifty years — my father farmed it before me, and I've seen all kinds of seasons on these 30 mu. Let me walk through what I'm planning.

---

**Wheat first — I'll be planting around October 10th.**

I do the same thing most years because it works. I don't have the energy to experiment at my age. I use hybrid wheat seed from the agricultural supply shop in town — the variety the shop recommends, usually one of the Jimai or Shimai series. About 15 kg of seed per mu, costs me around 40 yuan per mu.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before planting — about 40 kg per mu as base fertilizer. That gives me roughly 6 kg each of N, P, and K per mu at the start. Then in March when the wheat greens up and starts jointing, I topdress with urea — about 20 kg per mu, which is another 9 kg of N. So total about 15 kg N per mu across the season. The extension guy a few years ago said I could do less but I've always done it this way and I get 450-500 kg yield, so why change.

Irrigation — I have a tube well share with two neighbors. For wheat I irrigate before the ground freezes in November (the winter watering), then at green-up in March, and again at jointing, and usually one more at grain fill if it's dry. So 3-4 times depending on rain. Each watering costs me about 40 yuan per mu in electricity and pump fees.

I spray herbicide once in spring for weeds, and if I see aphids or rust at heading I'll do one insecticide-fungicide mix. 

Labor — my son is in Shijiazhuang working, doesn't come back for farming. It's just me and my wife. I can't do much heavy work anymore, so I hire the planter and harvester from the custom operator in the village. Costs money but there's no other way at my age.

I expect around 450 kg per mu. That's what I usually get. A good year I'll get 500, a bad year maybe 400.

---

**Maize — right after wheat harvest, mid-June.**

Very tight turnaround. The day the wheat comes off, the combine is barely out of the field and I need to get the maize in. I use no-till seeding — the neighbor down the road has a no-till planter with fertilizer applicator, I pay him to do it. This saves me from plowing, which I don't have time for anyway.

Hybrid maize seed — Zhengdan 958 or whatever is popular that year. About 35 yuan per mu for seed. I put down compound fertilizer as basal when planting — another 40 kg per mu, then at big trumpet stage (around late July) I topdress urea, maybe 15-18 kg per mu. Total N about 14-15 kg per mu.

Irrigation — maize needs water at tasseling if it's a dry July. Usually 1-2 times. Sometimes the rains come and I don't irrigate at all. This year I'll wait and see.

Herbicide once after planting to keep the weeds down. If armyworm shows up I spray, otherwise I don't.

Expected yield around 500 kg per mu. That's normal for around here.
